# Goban Studio v1.1.0

A release focused on the things v1.0 got wrong: the document-open path, honest
content counts, scoring at the board edge, package integrity, and the first
real look at the play surface.

## Download and first launch

| Platform | File | First launch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `GobanStudio-macOS-arm64.dmg` or `.zip` | Ad-hoc signed, **not notarized**. Right-click the app → Open once. If macOS still blocks it: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Goban\ Studio.app` |
| Windows (x64) | `GobanStudio-Windows-x64.zip` | **Not Authenticode-signed.** If SmartScreen appears, choose More info → Run anyway. WebView2 is preinstalled on Windows 10/11. |

Every release asset has a line in `SHA256SUMS`. The app is fully offline.

## Play

- **Both sidebars retract during a game.** The left navigation and the right
  game panel have independent buttons in the top bar; the choice is remembered.
  Review and Learn always open with their full layout.
- **The 19×19 board is the standard 19-line board.** The board grows into the
  space freed by the sidebars instead of staying capped at the old width.
- **Quieter shell.** Smaller type, hairline borders, no stacked card shadows,
  a single accent, and a cleaner top bar. The board is still the focus.
- Japanese rules only; komi, handicap, dead-stone scoring, pass, undo, resign
  and hint remain.

## Documents and records

- **Double-clicking an SGF now works on macOS and Windows.** macOS gets the
  missing Apple Event handler; Windows reads the path from its launch
  arguments. A file opened while the app is already running is picked up too.
- **A non-Japanese SGF is rejected with an explanation.** `RU[Chinese]`,
  Korean, AGA and other records are not silently re-scored as Japanese.
- **SGF export still writes `RU[Japanese]`**, with play, setup stones,
  comments, passes and variations.

## Content and scoring fixes

- **60 lessons are 60 distinct positions.** The reading lessons no longer
  repeat foundation positions; `star` now uses a 13×13 board and `atari-side`
  is a real side atari instead of a duplicate.
- **40 openings are 40 distinct titles and 40 distinct eight-move sequences.**
  Repeated player pairings carry their source date; the duplicated AlphaGo
  card is replaced with the actual game 1 record.
- **Territory is no longer decided by an arbitrary stone threshold.** A
  one-colour empty region counts only when it no longer reaches all four
  sides of the board. A lone stone or a wall with gaps is dame; a corner eye,
  side territory and a wall that really separates the board still count.
  Dead stones remain a manual confirmation, as Japanese rules require.
- **Review says what it is.** The curve is labelled a local shape/influence
  estimate, not KataGo win-rate analysis.

## Packaging

- The app's MIT licence and `@sabaki/go-board`'s MIT licence now ship inside
  every package, alongside Moka, KataGo and Inter notices.
- The Windows ZIP is written with `/` separators and Unix mode bits; the
  Windows job now launches the packaged GUI, checks the native bridge, and
  asks KataGo for a move before shipping.
- `SHA256SUMS` is published with the three assets.
- macOS and Windows install notes are inside the archives.

## Honest limits

- macOS notarization and Windows Authenticode require certificates that this
  project does not have. The packages remain ad-hoc/unsigned; the release and
  install notes now say so instead of leaving users to guess.
- Review is still the on-device estimate described above, not KataGo analysis.
- Japanese life-and-death is resolved by the player marking dead stones; the
  app does not claim to settle disputed positions automatically.

KataGo is MIT licensed. The bundled b6c96 network is distributed with KataGo.
